title: Decoding preserves the Boolean counter tape
statement: Let $e$ inject the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, let $x$ be an input over $\Gamma$, let $ip$ be a valid input-head position, and let $out$ be an output word over $\Gamma$. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, and suppose the tape $ct:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)$ based at $cp\in\mathbb Z$ stores the encoded word $w$ at every offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$. Form the configuration $D$ with input-head position $ip$, output $out$, work-tape content $ct$, work-tape head position $cp$, and state $\mathrm{run}$. Decoding $D$ leaves its state equal to $\mathrm{run}$, and its decoded work tape at each of those offsets equals the buffer-tape content of $w$ there.
hypotheses_covered: An injection $e$ from the Boolean alphabet to $\Gamma$
